A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM DNA work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original relationship-detection, model-routing, distance-correlation and phylogenetic results involving 305 LLMs.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, controlled fine-tuning experiments and extensive robustness analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same response generation, sentence embedding, concatenation and Gaussian projection procedure. RepTrace is a new name for the existing pipeline; alternative encoders and template settings are evaluated as ablations rather than introduced as a revised method.

E1.justification: v2 adds synthetic random-word inputs, mathematical fine-tuning using OpenMathInstruct-2, and relationship evaluation restricted to models sharing Qwen2Tokenizer. These substantially extend the tested conditions beyond the retained six extraction benchmarks, routing dataset and 305-model roster.

E2.justification: v1 compares relationship detection only against Random and Greedy. v2 adds PhyloLM distance signatures with an RBF-SVM in Table 1 and evaluates its same-tokenizer variant in Appendix C.7, introducing a directly relevant research comparator. The routing comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds accuracy reporting, alternative encoder configurations, template controls, embedding/DNA dimension sweeps, and full-parameter fine-tuning with 10–10,000 examples. New encoder-distance analyses sample 10,000 pairs. The model inventory also substantially revises reported parameter sizes, without establishing that model identities changed or existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Sections 5.5–5.7 and Appendices C.3–C.7 add tests of random-input robustness, chat templates, fine-tuning intensity, encoder choice, embedding dimension, DNA dimension, model-size bias and shared-tokenizer performance. The earlier dataset-stability test, phylogenetic analysis and false-positive case study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed means and standard deviations; no increased run count is documented. v2 adds Spearman-based encoder-distance comparisons and point-biserial correlation plus logistic-regression significance testing for model-size effects.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises existing scores: Qwen3-based DNA AUC changes from 0.957 ± 0.044 to 0.979 ± 0.027, while the newly evaluated BGE variant reports 0.992 ± 0.023. Random and Greedy scores also change. New robustness and fine-tuning results substantially expand the evidence; Table 2 routing scores remain identical.

T1.justification: v2 introduces Definition A.1, formally defining evolution as an operation bounded in Hilbert distance. The existing DNA definition, inheritance and determinism theorems, existence argument, projection corollary and concentration proof are otherwise retained through relocation and renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: a bi-Lipschitz functional representation, its existence and biological analogues, training-free extraction, relationship detection and phylogenetic reconstruction. The new experiments primarily support these existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning input and encoder robustness, template fairness, fine-tuning effects and model-size independence. Appendices D–E substantially expand applicability and limitations, including governance, risk tracing, adaptive attacks, contamination and uninterpreted DNA subsequences. Appendix C.7 also qualifies the comparison with PhyloLM's intended tasks.

D1.justification: v2 adds source-code, interactive-demo and PyPI access/install information, alongside specifications for the new experiments. Model-size documentation is extensively revised: for example, Mixtral-8x7B changes from 7.0B to 47B, and previously unknown Flan-T5 sizes are supplied. These are documented changes, not independently verified corrections.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around PhyloLM, explaining its tokenizer-dependent distances and contrasting them with sentence-level DNA representations. It replaces v1's assertion that no existing method reliably handles the heterogeneous comparison. Related work also expands to HybridLLM and MetaLLM, with additional literature supporting the broader-impact discussion.

P1.justification: v2 consolidates definition and existence into one section, moves inheritance/determinism and Hilbert-space development into Appendix A, and reorganizes the appendices, including a separate model-details section. Related-work and experimental narratives are substantially expanded, and the extraction pipeline receives the name RepTrace.

P2.justification: v2 adds a fine-tuning heatmap, encoder-distance plots, two dimension-sensitivity figures and four result tables. Table 1 gains an accuracy column and additional method rows. Existing displays are reflowed; the earlier phylogenetic figures are retained as Figures 6–7 rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The PhyloLM comparisons and systematic extraction controls address important weaknesses in v1's baseline coverage and largely untested configuration choices. Access information and explicit limitations further strengthen the paper. Some new interpretations overreach: Section 5.7 claims monotonic growth although Figure 5 falls from 0.7860 to 0.7001 between 100 and 1,000 examples, and Appendix C.6 treats nonsignificance as proof of independence. These weaken particular conclusions, but the overall validation is substantially stronger.
